newsitem.title: USA: Greenspan Q&A -- Taxes and budget deal, Part VIII.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan Q&A -- Taxes and budget deal, Part VIII.

text.p: Following are excerpts from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's question-and-answer session the Senate Banking Committee with after the second day of his semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony.

Sen. Kerry (D-Mass) - "Looking at this budget deal ... Would you look at the spending levels and say they're too high, they're too low? Would you look at the tax cuts .. Are they too high, too low or sufficient? How would you size up this budget?

Grenspan: "As a technical matter you cannot balance budgets over the long run by raising taxes because the very profit itself will inhibit income growth, reduce revenues and indeed end up counter-productive.
"The only way to address a long-term strutural budget deficit problem is through the expenditure side. It's the only way that you'll succeed in a permanent manner."
